assessment.overall: architecture works; target coordination and future-position utility remain limiting

strengths: all kobolds established protected ambush positions
all kobolds spent one Hidden opening attack
all ogres used full-speed charge plans
pressure changed the ranged side into fighting withdrawal
no actor entered a hazard or attacked with a range penalty
failures: five kobolds discarded most or all of round 2 to avoid a minus-two shot
ambush target assignment oscillated from Ogre 2 or 4 to Ogre 6, Ogre 1 and Ogre 5
all six kobolds received the same Ogre 6 target in round 2 regardless of lane
kobold damage spread over four ogres and removed none
withdrawal routes approached map edges and did not forecast the enemy next turn
opening ambush remained strategically dominant after melee pressure became urgent
ogres sometimes reserved more expected damage than a target could survive
priorities: sticky lane-aware target assignment with expected-damage reservations
turn-horizon comparison of penalized ambush fire against waiting
multi-turn escape-route scoring with edge and dead-end repulsion
pressure override for unfinished opening assignments
simulation parity for javelin draw and ammunition
